title: 3-week surge sprint: KPI tactician & readiness checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a tactical, compact playbook for a time-boxed 3-week surge sprint designed to validate scaling strategies for a new hosted inference feature. Focus: latency-sensitive customers and first 100k requests.

Audience:
Product Ops, Eng SRE, Serving Runtime, Console & Rollouts, Solutions Eng.

High-level objective:
- Deliver controlled ramp to 100k requests/day on hosted API with latency 95th <= 220ms for p50 model class.
- Validate Dedicated fallback behavior and routing policies.
- Produce a final go/no-go recommendation and checklist for wider rollout.

Sprint structure (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep, short): config freeze, smoke tests, traffic staging lanes created.
- Week 1 (pilot): 5k -> 25k/day (selected customers, feature flags).
- Week 2 (ramp): 25k -> 70k/day (wider cohort, canary A/B).
- Week 3 (stress & verify): 70k -> 100k/day, soak and postmortem.

KPI tracker (single source of truth fields) — update daily in the sheet: 
- date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- ingress_qps (requests/sec) 
- avg_latency_ms (rolling 1m p50)
- latency_p95_ms (rolling 1m)
- error_rate_pct (5xx + timeouts / total)
- successful_tokens_per_second (tokens/s)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd (estimated)
- cache_hit_rate_pct (prefix/KV caches)
- batch_size_avg (effective)
- routing_fallbacks (count)
- active_customers_in_cohort (count)
- ops_incidents (ticket ids comma-separated)
- owner_oncall (name)

Thresholds & triggers (operational):
- Immediate alert: latency_p95_ms > 300ms OR error_rate_pct > 2% -> page SRE oncall + product-ops lead.
- Investigate: latency_p95_ms between 220-300ms OR error_rate_pct 1-2% -> slack triage channel, reduce traffic by 30% to pilot lane.
- Auto-throttle: sustained ingress_qps above planned for >10m with no scaling headroom -> routing policy should cut non-critical tenants by 20%.

Owner map (roles & escalation):
- Lead: Aisha Chen (product-ops) — overall go/no-go and customer comms.
- Runtime engineer: Marco Alvarez — kernel selection, model variant mapping.
- SRE: Priya Singh — autoscaling policy, incident commander.
- Console/Telemetry: Liam O'Connor — dashboards, alert rules, sampling.
- Solutions Eng: Sora Tanaka — customer coordination + targeted rollbacks.

Readiness checklist (pre-deploy items) — MUST be green before pilot:
- [ ] Config freeze applied to routing and rollout infra. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Canary bucket created and verified (traffic shaping). (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Autoscaler test run at 2x expected QPS. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Model variants pinned & quant profiles validated. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] KV/prefix cache primed for pilot dataset. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Billing/cost meter dashboard enabled for cohort. (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Customer comms template drafted for pilot participants. (owner: Sora)
- [ ] Rollback playbook rehearsed and smoke-tested. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Observability sampling enabled (trace + token-level cost). (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Compliance checklist for pilot tenant data (consent + retention). (owner: Aisha)

Launch-day checklist (pilot ramp):
T-minus 30m:
- [ ] Confirm oncall roster and escalation Slack bridge is open.
- [ ] Final metric baseline snapshot taken.
- [ ] Alerting rules set to pilot sensitivity.
T-minus 5m:
- [ ] Toggle feature flag to pilot cohort (monitor for 60s).
- [ ] Confirm p50/p95 latency at 1m window.
+60m:
- [ ] Confirm cache warm rates and KV hit-rate >= 40%.
- [ ] Check routing fallbacks = 0.

Contingency playbook (if thresholds exceed):
1) Immediate mitigation (0-15m): rollback flag -> reduce cohort traffic by 50% -> apply emergency autoscaler clamp -> notify customers.
2) Short-term (15-120m): increase dedicated pool (if available) -> redirect high-p50 tenants -> enable lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical traffic.
3) Post-incident (next 24-72h): postmortem, action items, change to rollout heuristics.

Experiment matrix (things to try during ramp):
- Batch-size tuning: test target batch sizes of 4, 8, 16 with continuous batching; measure tokens/s and latency.
- Cache policies: prefix-only vs prefix+kv full warmups.
- Routing heuristics: latency-first vs cost-first policy (50/50 split A/B).
- Quant variants: int8 vs fp16 for tail-latency sensitive models.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How many pilot tenants are comfortable with short 10-15 minute interruptions? (ask Sora to confirm).
- Need a small synthetic traffic harness that simulates 95th% user story (characteristics: sporadic bursts, many small requests). PR exists: github PR/77 but still needs scale test.
- Confirm billing metric tags will appear in tenant-level invoices (finance).

Quick links and refs:
- Ramp runbook (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-PLN-8421
- Relevant PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/77
- Pilot signups sheet: drive://sheets/pilot-cohort-2026-q1
- Incident template: CONFLUENCE-OPS-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE

Daily update format for standup (copy into slack thread):
- Day X: ingress_qps / p50 / p95 / error% / cache_hit% / action_taken / owner

Post-sprint deliverables:
- Final KPI ledger exported to csv, annotated with incidents and mitigations.
- Go/no-go recommendation with 3 rollout scenarios + cost delta.
- Playbook updates (move items from draft -> final).

Bottom line summary (TL;DR):
This doc is the tactical guide for a short, observable surge experiment focused on latency and routing resiliency. Keep rollouts small, instrument aggressively, and have a practiced rollback sequence. The goal is to prove the economics and reliability assumptions before a broad activation.

-- Aisha (draft)

Unresolved action items (append to sheet):

- Marco: autoscaler tweak PR for kernel selection (due 2026-02-25)
- Priya: rehearse rollback in staging with 3rd-party load generator (due 2026-02-26)

End of doc.
